title: The character has a role. The user should have one too.
intro: Emotional connection also depends on how a person is recognized within the story. Persona settings give the user a way to describe who they are, with a reusable default and a separate persona for an individual character.

blocks.alt: Talkie Persona Card editor with a Default label, name, gender and Who I Am fields
blocks.caption: The editor makes the scope visible: this card is the default applied across chats.

blocks.label: ONE MODEL, TWO SCOPES
blocks.title: Make reuse and specificity understandable.
body: A default persona can carry across chats; a character-specific persona supports a different role in a particular story. Labels and separate entries make that distinction visible.
The mobile design carries the same distinction into the character panel. The interaction notes cover first creation, editing an existing persona, and making a new persona the default for all chats.

figure.alt: Mobile character panel showing Default persona and a separate persona for Arlene McCoy
figure.caption: Mobile web · Default and character-specific personas remain distinct.

blocks.label: DESIGN TRADEOFF
blocks.text: A reusable identity saves repetition. A local override leaves room to play a different role.
